From around December to March the north-west monsoon brings humid air, more rain and generally lighter winds from the north-west. From around May to October the south-east trades blow steadily from the opposite direction: cooler, drier and breezier, strongest in the middle of the year. April and November, between the two, are often the calmest months of all.

From roughly December to March the north-west monsoon makes north- and west-facing coasts choppier. From roughly May to October the south-east trades do the same to south- and east-facing coasts. April and November, in between, are usually calm almost everywhere.

The Aldabra giant tortoise is one of the largest tortoises in the world. Its home atoll, Aldabra, holds by far the biggest wild population; elsewhere you will meet tortoises roaming free on Curieuse, on Bird Island and in gardens and small reserves across the inner islands.

The Seychelles are not one beach. They are granite mountains and palm forests, coral cays and far-off atolls, each with its own pace. We plan journeys through several of them, slowly enough to notice the difference.

The Vallée de Mai is a palm forest in the middle of Praslin, protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and managed by the Seychelles Islands Foundation. It is one of only two places where the coco de mer grows wild: the other is neighbouring Curieuse.

The best place to see it is the Vallée de Mai on Praslin, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The trails are well kept and shaded, and the giant fronds overhead clatter in the wind. It is also home to the Seychelles black parrot, which is easier to hear than to see. Fond Ferdinand, a smaller reserve in the south-east of the island, also protects coco de mer palms and is usually quieter.

The coco de mer is protected. Nuts can only be exported legally with an official certificate and permit, sold through licensed outlets. Check the current rules before you buy.

The coco de mer produces the largest seed in the plant kingdom, and it grows wild only on Praslin and Curieuse. Everything about it is slow: the nuts take years to mature, and young palms take many years more before they bear fruit.

The coco de mer produces the largest seed of any plant. Male and female trees are separate; the nuts take years to mature, and a palm can live for centuries. Walking under the fronds, many metres overhead, is the closest thing the islands have to a cathedral.
